title: Exploring Some Geometric Themes: Fractals, Views and Solids
seo_title: Exploring Some Geometric Themes Class 8 Worksheet with Answers (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 4)
standard_code: Class 8, Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 4: Exploring Some Geometric Themes
standard_text: Fractals such as the Sierpinski triangle and carpet, visualising 3-D shapes from different views, and faces, edges and vertices of polyhedra with Euler's formula (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 8)
meta_desc: Class 8 Exploring Some Geometric Themes worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 4): Sierpinski fractals, top, front and side views, faces, edges and vertices, Euler's formula. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Euler's formula holds for every polyhedron, such as a cube: 6 + 8 − 12 = 2.
body_html:
How it works

A fractal repeats the same rule at smaller and smaller sizes. In the Sierpinski triangle each step keeps 3 of 4 smaller triangles, so the count is 3n and the area left is (3/4)n.

A solid can be drawn from the top, front and side.

For a polyhedron, faces F, vertices V and edges E satisfy F + V − E = 2. A prism on an n-sided base has n + 2 faces, 2n vertices and 3n edges.

Example

How many edges does a hexagonal prism have?

n = 6

3n = 18

Answer: 18

Example

A solid has 8 faces and 12 vertices. How many edges?

E = F + V − 2

Answer: 18

Common mistakes

  • Adding 3 each step in the Sierpinski triangle instead of multiplying by 3.
  • Mixing up vertices (corners) and edges (lines).
  • Drawing the front view when the top view is asked.
